policy: Advisory only. Actual source equations, type-class scope and numeric policy override these entries. Compilation replay is not semantic proof. Unreviewed mined candidates are never loaded.

entries.title: IBig has no magnitude method in dashu-int 0.6.2
entries.preconditions: Receiver is IBig; this source operation needs an owned natural magnitude only after a nonnegative guard. The historical full run was interrupted; only compilation replay passed.
entries.guidance: into_parts(self) yields (Sign, UBig). Move when ownership permits; clone only if the original borrowed IBig must survive. For magnitude bit length alone use the verified BitTest::bit_len API instead.
entries.forbidden_shortcuts: Do not replace signed-to-natural truncation by absolute value; negative values still map to zero under the recorded source guard.
entries.example: if i < &IBig::ZERO { UBig::ZERO } else { let (_, magnitude)=i.clone().into_parts(); magnitude }

entries.title: Use after move
entries.preconditions: A value is used after an owning operation; inspect all live callers and branches.
entries.guidance: For read-only reuse borrow; consume/destructure only when the old value is dead. Clone only if an independently owned duplicate is required and the source type permits it.
entries.forbidden_shortcuts: Do not add Clone/Copy bounds to a polymorphic export merely to satisfy a concrete test.
entries.example: let n = xs.len(); consume(xs); use_len(n); // only if source needs length, not xs

entries.title: Unsatisfied trait obligation
entries.preconditions: The diagnostic identifies a concrete missing trait on the actual generic type.
entries.guidance: Trace the required operation to source type-class constraints. Implement the justified operation or revise representation/call shape; propagate only source-authorized bounds.
entries.forbidden_shortcuts: Do not narrow all source type variables to Clone, Copy, Ord or a test-only numeric type.
entries.example: fn compare<T: PartialEq>(a: &T,b: &T)->bool { a == b } // requires source equality capability

entries.title: Type mismatch
entries.preconditions: Inspect expected and found types including references, aliases, Result and source numeric meaning.
entries.guidance: Repair the producer/consumer boundary; use explicit fallible conversion only when range/overflow policy requires it.
entries.forbidden_shortcuts: Do not use as, unwrap or clone as a universal coercion; changing the return ownership may break callers.
entries.example: let n = usize::try_from(count)?; // only after source range/boundary analysis

entries.title: Overlapping mutable borrows
entries.preconditions: Two exclusive borrows overlap in lifetime.
entries.guidance: Separate read/update scopes or use a proven disjoint split when source access/order permits; inspect captured borrows.
entries.forbidden_shortcuts: Do not use unsafe aliases or clone whole structures to hide ownership mistakes.
entries.example: let (left,right)=xs.split_at_mut(k); // k checked; operations require disjoint regions

entries.title: Conflicting shared and exclusive borrows
entries.preconditions: A live shared borrow overlaps an exclusive borrow.
entries.guidance: Compute needed scalar facts before the update or end the shared borrow before mutation when source order permits.
entries.forbidden_shortcuts: Do not reorder observable callbacks or discard persistent old versions.

entries.title: Borrow outlives value
entries.preconditions: The referenced local is dropped while a borrow can still be used.
entries.guidance: Move ownership to an appropriate lifetime scope or return an owned value when the source interface requires ownership.
entries.forbidden_shortcuts: Do not leak allocations or fabricate static lifetimes.

entries.title: Unavailable method
entries.preconditions: Check the concrete receiver, dependency version and imported traits.
entries.guidance: Inspect the locked API. Distinguish a missing trait import, wrong receiver, and nonexistent method; do not invent APIs.
entries.forbidden_shortcuts: Do not add unrelated traits or change source operations solely to obtain a similarly named method.
entries.example: Import the actual defining trait only after verifying its implementation for this receiver.

entries.preconditions: Read the actual typed source equations, not just the bit-operation class name; each concrete instance needs its own boundary cases.
entries.guidance: Resolve feasible small results before narrowing a mathematical count to usize: natural take with count >= magnitude length returns the operand; signed floor drop at such a count returns 0 or -1; zero push remains zero. Negative take/nonzero push may need a huge result. Checked shifts must validate lost high bits, not merely count.
entries.forbidden_shortcuts: Never reduce the count modulo native width or treat a failed count conversion as proof that the result overflows. Library magnitude bit length is not HOL negative bitlen.
entries.example: drop_bit huge_count (-1) = -1 under signed floor semantics; push_bit huge_count 0 = 0.

entries.preconditions: The extracted source contains a typed List.list constructor; inspect each affected source equation and its observations.
entries.guidance: Vec preserves sequence order and multiplicity. Borrow a slice for read-only access when callers retain ownership; move elements only when old values are unobserved. A set or deduplicating worklist needs source justification for every affected operation.
entries.forbidden_shortcuts: Do not infer that order/duplicates are irrelevant from one membership-only caller or from task names.
entries.example: [a,a] and [a] remain distinct list values unless the source proves the observation identifies them.
